items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 31:1
items.html: Mazal is from the language of the verse, "water shall drip from his branches [yizlu mayim midalyav]," which is a language of bestowal. And since the eighth correction is the totality of the seven corrections of the beard preceding it, therefore it is fit for bestowal and is called Mazal. And likewise the thirteenth correction is the totality of the perfection in the four corrections preceding it, and it too is fit for bestowal, and it too is called Mazal. Only, the eighth Mazal, being the totality of the perfection of the seven upper corrections of Hochma, is called the upper Mazal. And the thirteenth Mazal, being the totality of the perfection of the four lower corrections, which are drawn from the Galgalta, is therefore called the lower Mazal. (Item 212).
